title: Cloud Consulting Karachi: AWS, Azure, Google | 22 Signals
description: Cloud consulting Karachi banks, fintechs and enterprises need: architecture, security and cost reviews on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, planned around SBP rules.
h1: Cloud consulting Karachi businesses can defend to their regulator and their CFO
intro: We give Karachi companies cloud consulting that covers architecture, security, monitoring and cost on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure. For banks, fintechs and insurers we plan workloads around State Bank of Pakistan cloud outsourcing rules. For everyone else we focus on uptime, sensible access control and a monthly bill that matches what the business actually uses.

sections.h: Why cloud decisions are harder in Karachi
p: A cloud decision for a Karachi company is never just technical. Finance asks why the cloud bill, charged in dollars, keeps rising while revenue is earned in rupees. Compliance asks where customer data physically sits. Operations remembers the last time a submarine cable fault slowed international traffic, or a power cut took the server room down, and wants to know what happens next time.

Each question has a good answer, but only if someone designs for all of them together. That is the job: an architecture that is secure, resilient and sensible to run in rupee terms, with the paperwork your board and regulator expect.

Many Karachi IT estates grew one server at a time: an ERP box in the office, a website on shared hosting, a mobile app backend on a developer's personal cloud account. Good cloud consulting Karachi companies can rely on starts by finding all of it, putting it under company-owned accounts and deciding what stays, what moves and what is switched off.

list: Architecture design on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure, including hybrid setups with an existing data centre.
Workload placement: which systems belong in a nearby hyperscaler region, which in a Pakistan-based facility and which on premises.
Security and access control: identity, least-privilege roles, encryption, key management and audit logging.
Monitoring and alerting so problems reach a person before customers notice.
Backup, disaster recovery and failover plans, tested rather than assumed.
Cost reviews: rightsizing, reserved capacity, storage tiers and removing forgotten resources.
Managed cloud operations if you would rather not run it in-house.

sections.h: State Bank of Pakistan rules and the cloud
p: For banks, microfinance banks, electronic money institutions and other regulated entities, the State Bank's framework on outsourcing to cloud service providers sets the ground rules: how workloads are classified, what due diligence is required on the provider, what approvals and notifications apply, and how data and access are controlled. Material workloads face stricter conditions than non-material ones.

We help your technology and compliance teams classify each workload, document the provider assessment and design controls that match. Insurers and NBFCs supervised by the SECP have their own expectations, which we cover in the same exercise. The regulatory filing and final sign-off remain yours and your advisers'.

list: Banks and fintechs on I.I. Chundrigar Road and beyond moving digital channels, analytics or internal tools to the cloud.
Insurers modernising policy and claims systems.
Logistics and shipping firms that need tracking systems and client portals to stay up around the clock.
FMCG and manufacturing groups consolidating ERP, reporting and email across plants and offices.
E-commerce and retail brands whose traffic spikes during Ramadan, Eid and seasonal sales.
Media companies storing and distributing large video libraries.

sections.h: How it works: Talk, Plan, Build, Grow
p: Talk: we review what you run today, what it costs and what keeps your IT team up at night.
Plan: an architecture document, a workload placement map, a security design and a cost model, all in writing.
Build: we set up the accounts, networks, identity, monitoring and pipelines, then move or deploy workloads in agreed stages.
Grow: monthly cost and security reviews, and changes as the business adds products or users. For larger moves, our Cloud Migration service handles the cutover plan.

sections.h: Proof: dates that do not move
p: We have run and broadcast more than 20 large-scale live events. The lesson from live work applies directly to cloud cutovers: the date does not move, so the rehearsal, the rollback plan and the checklist have to be right beforehand. We plan infrastructure changes the same way.

Your Karachi project runs under one Signal Lead. Cloud work is done in the console and in code, and every planned change goes into a calendar agreed with your team. We schedule maintenance windows and cutovers for your quiet hours, with a rollback step written down before anything moves.
Access is granted through your own identity system with named accounts and logging, and is removed when the work ends. If a data-centre visit or workshop on site is needed, we plan it for that stage.

faqs.q: Which cloud is best for a Karachi company: AWS, Azure or Google Cloud?
faqs.a: There is no single answer. Azure often suits firms already deep in Microsoft 365. AWS has the widest service range. Google Cloud is strong for data and analytics. We compare them on your workloads, regulatory needs, latency to your users and running cost in your currency, then recommend one, or a mix, in writing.

faqs.q: Can a Pakistani bank use public cloud?
faqs.a: Yes, within the State Bank of Pakistan's framework on outsourcing to cloud service providers. The framework distinguishes material from non-material workloads and sets due diligence, approval and control requirements. We help you classify workloads and prepare the technical evidence. Your compliance team and the SBP make the final call.

faqs.q: Will our data be stored in Pakistan?
faqs.a: That depends on the workload and your policy. Some data can sit in a hyperscaler region outside the country, while some may need to stay in Pakistan under regulatory or contractual rules. We map each data set to an approved location and document it, so the answer is clear for auditors and customers.

faqs.q: How do you cut our cloud bill?
faqs.a: We start with a cost review: unused resources, oversized servers, storage on the wrong tier and capacity that could be reserved. Most savings come from those basics. Then we set budgets and alerts so the bill stays visible. We report what changed and why, without touching anything you have not approved.

faqs.q: What does the cloud consulting Karachi teams get from us look like day to day?
faqs.a: Your Signal Lead runs a weekly call at a time agreed with your team and shares progress in writing. Engineers work through named, logged accounts on your systems. Cutovers are scheduled for your quiet hours. If something needs a person on site, we arrange it for that stage.

faqs.q: Do you offer ongoing cloud support?
faqs.a: Yes. Managed cloud operations cover monitoring, patching, backups, security reviews and monthly cost reports, with agreed response times. Some companies keep an in-house team for daily tasks and use us for architecture, reviews and escalations. We scope whichever model fits.
